intro: En C1 el inglés deja de ser una traducción del español: aprendes a dar énfasis como un nativo, a deducir sobre el pasado, a elegir el registro adecuado, a evitar repeticiones con elipsis y a combinar palabras como lo hacen los hablantes cultos. Diez lecciones y un examen con el temario de los exámenes oficiales de nivel C1.
goals: Dar énfasis con la inversión (Not only…, Rarely…, Never…).
Destacar una parte de la frase con oraciones hendidas (It was… who, What I need is…).
Deducir sobre el pasado con must have, can't have, might have y should have.
Elegir el registro: formal e informal, y las colocaciones que suenan naturales.
Evitar repeticiones con elipsis y sustitución (so do I, do so, neither).
Dominar los verbos que cambian de sentido con -ing o infinitivo.
Graduar la probabilidad (bound to, likely to, may well).
Adelantar elementos para dar énfasis (fronting) y nominalizar en textos formales.
Usar preposiciones dependientes y expresiones fijas con naturalidad.

lessons.title: La inversión: Not only…, Rarely…, Never…
lessons.summary: Cuando el adverbio negativo va primero, el verbo se adelanta al sujeto.

sections.heading: Adverbios negativos al principio
body: Para dar énfasis, una expresión negativa o restrictiva puede ir al inicio; entonces el auxiliar se coloca delante del sujeto, como en una pregunta: Never have I seen such a mess (= I have never seen…). Rarely do we eat out. Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
Si no hay auxiliar, se añade do/does/did: Seldom does he complain.

examples.en: Never have I been so embarrassed.
examples.es: Nunca me he sentido tan avergonzado.

examples.en: Rarely do we get such good weather in March.
examples.es: Rara vez tenemos tan buen tiempo en marzo.

examples.en: Not only did he apologise, but he also offered to pay.
examples.es: No solo se disculpó, sino que también se ofreció a pagar.

examples.en: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
examples.es: Bajo ninguna circunstancia debes abrir esta puerta.

examples.en: Little did they know what was coming.
examples.es: Poco sabían lo que se avecinaba.

examples.en: At no time was the public in danger.
examples.es: En ningún momento estuvo el público en peligro.

rows: Never had she felt so free.
Not only is it cheap, but it's also fast.
No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.
Hardly had we left when it started to rain.
Under no circumstances must you tell him.

sections.heading: No sooner, hardly y only
body: No sooner had… than y hardly had… when cuentan dos hechos casi simultáneos, con pasado perfecto en la primera parte. Only after, only when, only then también invierten, pero en la oración principal: Only when she left did I notice the note.

examples.en: No sooner had the show started than the lights went out.
examples.es: Apenas había empezado el espectáculo cuando se fueron las luces.

examples.en: Hardly had I arrived when they asked me to leave.
examples.es: Apenas había llegado cuando me pidieron que me fuera.

examples.en: Only after the meeting did we realise the mistake.
examples.es: Solo después de la reunión nos dimos cuenta del error.

sections.tip: La inversión es formal o literaria: en una charla relajada se dice I've never seen…; en un discurso o un texto, Never have I seen….

sections.heading: Inversión en condicionales formales
body: En registro formal, if puede desaparecer con inversión: Had I known (= If I had known), Should you need help (= If you need help), Were it not for (= If it weren't for).

examples.en: Had we known about the delay, we would have taken another route.
examples.es: De haber sabido del retraso, habríamos tomado otra ruta.

examples.en: Should you have any questions, please contact us.
examples.es: Si tiene alguna pregunta, contáctenos.

examples.en: Were I in your position, I would accept.
examples.es: Si yo estuviera en tu posición, aceptaría.

exercises.prompt: Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.
exercises.explanation: Tras never al inicio, el auxiliar va delante del sujeto.

exercises.prompt: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.
Rarely ___ we see him these days. (auxiliar)
exercises.explanation: Sin auxiliar propio, se añade do.

exercises.prompt: No sooner ___ I closed the door than I remembered the keys. (auxiliar)

exercises.es: Solo entonces entendí el problema.
De haberlo sabido, te habría avisado.
answers: Had I known, I would have warned you.
Had I known, I would have told you.
Had I known, I'd have warned you.
Had I known, I'd have told you.

exercises.prompt: Little ___ that it was the last time.

exercises.es: En ningún momento estuvo en peligro.
answers: At no time was he in danger.
At no time was she in danger.
At no time was it in danger.

lessons.title: Oraciones hendidas: It was… who, What I need is…
lessons.summary: Mover el foco a la parte de la frase que importa.

sections.heading: It + be + … + who / that
body: Para destacar un elemento se envuelve con it was… that/who: Ana broke the vase → It was Ana who broke the vase (fue Ana, no otra persona). It was yesterday that I saw him (fue ayer, no otro día).

examples.en: It was my sister who told me.
examples.es: Fue mi hermana quien me lo dijo.

examples.en: It's the price that worries me, not the quality.
examples.es: Es el precio lo que me preocupa, no la calidad.

examples.en: It was in Lisbon that we first met.
examples.es: Fue en Lisboa donde nos conocimos.

sections.heading: What + oración + be
body: What I need is a holiday (lo que necesito son vacaciones). What + sujeto + verbo + be + lo destacado. También con all: All I want is some peace (lo único que quiero es paz). Y con the reason / the place / the thing: The reason I called is that…

examples.en: What she loves most is travelling.
examples.es: Lo que más le gusta es viajar.

examples.en: What happened was that the car broke down.
examples.es: Lo que pasó fue que el coche se averió.

examples.en: All we need is a little more time.
examples.es: Lo único que necesitamos es un poco más de tiempo.

examples.en: The reason I'm late is that the train was cancelled.
examples.es: La razón por la que llego tarde es que cancelaron el tren.

examples.en: What matters is that you tried.
examples.es: Lo que importa es que lo intentaste.

examples.en: It's not the money that bothers me; it's the attitude.
examples.es: No es el dinero lo que me molesta; es la actitud.

rows: The reason is that it's cheap.

sections.heading: Énfasis con do y con repetición
body: Do/does/did delante del verbo refuerza una afirmación: I do like your idea. She did call, but you were out. Y en respuestas a una duda: It does work.

examples.en: I do understand your concern.
examples.es: Sí que entiendo tu preocupación.

examples.en: He did try to help.
examples.es: Él sí intentó ayudar.

sections.tip: El do enfático se pronuncia con fuerza: I DO like it.

exercises.prompt: ___ my brother who fixed the computer.
___ I really want is a quiet weekend.
It was in 2010 ___ we moved here. (that)
All she ___ was listen. (verbo en pasado)

exercises.es: Lo que necesito es un café.
Fue Ana quien rompió el jarrón.
answers: It was Ana who broke the vase.
It was Ana that broke the vase.

exercises.prompt: ___ really annoyed me was his silence.

exercises.es: Es la actitud lo que me molesta.
answers: It's the attitude that bothers me.
It is the attitude that bothers me.
It's the attitude that annoys me.

lessons.title: Modales perfectos: must have, can't have, should have
lessons.summary: Deducir, lamentar y criticar sobre el pasado.

sections.heading: Deducir sobre el pasado
body: Modal + have + participio. Must have: casi seguro que pasó (She must have missed the bus). Can't have / couldn't have: casi seguro que no pasó (He can't have forgotten: it was his idea). Might have / may have / could have: es posible que pasara (They might have got lost).

examples.en: The ground is wet. It must have rained last night.
examples.es: El suelo está mojado. Debió de llover anoche.

examples.en: She can't have seen me; she didn't say hello.
examples.es: No puede haberme visto; no saludó.

examples.en: He may have left already.
examples.es: Puede que ya se haya ido.

examples.en: They could have taken the wrong exit.
examples.es: Podrían haber tomado la salida equivocada.

examples.en: She might have missed the train; she's usually on time.
examples.es: Puede que haya perdido el tren; suele ser puntual.

examples.en: You must have been very proud.
examples.es: Debiste de sentirte muy orgulloso.

sections.heading: Lamentar y criticar: should have y needn't have
body: Should have + participio: algo que era lo correcto y no se hizo (I should have called you), o lo contrario con shouldn't have (You shouldn't have said that). Needn't have + participio: se hizo sin necesidad (You needn't have brought a gift). Could have + participio también sirve de reproche: You could have told me!

examples.en: I should have studied more.
examples.es: Debería haber estudiado más.

examples.en: You shouldn't have spent so much.
examples.es: No deberías haber gastado tanto.

examples.en: We needn't have hurried; the train was late.
examples.es: No hacía falta que corriéramos; el tren llegó tarde.

examples.en: You could have warned me!
examples.es: ¡Podrías haberme avisado!

sections.tip: Should have se contrae en la lengua hablada a should've: nunca se escribe «should of».

sections.heading: Would have: lo que habría pasado
body: Would have + participio es la consecuencia del tercer condicional y también expresa suposición sobre el pasado: I would have helped, but I wasn't there. Con otros modales: would rather have (habría preferido).

examples.en: I would have come, but nobody told me.
examples.es: Habría venido, pero nadie me avisó.

examples.en: She would have been about thirty then.
examples.es: Ella tendría unos treinta años entonces.

exercises.prompt: The lights were on all night. They ___ forgotten to switch them off.
You ___ told me earlier! Now it's too late.
He ___ (can't / forget) the meeting; I reminded him twice.
We ___ (needn't / bring) food; there was plenty.

exercises.es: Ella debió de perder el tren.
Debería haber escuchado a mi madre.
answers: I should have listened to my mother.
I should've listened to my mother.
I should have listened to my mum.

exercises.prompt: I ___ my keys at the office; I can't find them anywhere.

exercises.es: No deberías haber dicho eso.
answers: You should not have said that.

lessons.title: Registro y colocaciones
lessons.summary: Decir lo mismo en formal y en informal, y combinar palabras como un nativo.

sections.heading: Formal e informal
body: El inglés formal prefiere verbos de origen latino (purchase, require, inform) frente a los phrasal verbs del habla cotidiana (buy, need, let know); evita contracciones y usa pasivas y estructuras impersonales (It is recommended that…). Un correo a una empresa y un mensaje a un amigo no comparten vocabulario.

examples.en: I would be grateful if you could send me the invoice. / Can you send me the bill?
examples.es: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura. / ¿Me pasas la cuenta?

examples.en: We regret to inform you that… / Sorry, but…
examples.es: Lamentamos comunicarle que… / Lo siento, pero…

examples.en: Please do not hesitate to contact us. / Just give us a shout.
examples.es: No dude en contactarnos. / Avísanos sin problema.

sections.heading: Colocaciones: palabras que van juntas
body: Una colocación es una combinación habitual: make a decision (no «take a decision»), heavy rain (no «strong rain»), fast food pero quick meal, do homework, make a mistake, pay attention, catch a cold, keep a promise, highly unlikely, deeply sorry, fully aware.

examples.en: She made a quick decision.
examples.es: Ella tomó una decisión rápida.

examples.en: We had heavy rain all week.
examples.es: Tuvimos lluvias fuertes toda la semana.

examples.en: Pay attention to the details.
examples.es: Presta atención a los detalles.

examples.en: I'm fully aware of the risks.
examples.es: Soy plenamente consciente de los riesgos.

examples.en: We need to take responsibility for our mistakes.
examples.es: Tenemos que asumir la responsabilidad de nuestros errores.

examples.en: The talks made little progress.
examples.es: Las conversaciones avanzaron poco.

rows: a decision, a mistake, an effort, progress, friends
homework, business, research, your best, the shopping
a photo, a break, a risk, responsibility, place
a look, a rest, an argument, fun, a go
a promise, a secret, in touch, calm

sections.tip: Make o do: make crea algo o decide (make a plan, make a decision); do es la actividad en sí (do the dishes, do research).

sections.heading: Suavizar y precisar: hedging
body: Para no sonar tajante: It seems that…, It appears…, This may suggest…, to some extent, arguably, perhaps, I would argue that…. Para precisar: in particular, specifically, namely.

examples.en: It seems that the figures are incomplete.
examples.es: Parece que las cifras están incompletas.

examples.en: This is, to some extent, a matter of taste.
examples.es: Esto es, en cierta medida, cuestión de gustos.

examples.en: Arguably, the second film is better.
examples.es: Podría decirse que la segunda película es mejor.

exercises.prompt: Formal: We ___ the meeting until next week.
She ___ a serious mistake.
Please ___ attention to the instructions. (verbo)
It's ___ unlikely that they will come. (muy, con un adverbio que colocaciona con unlikely)

exercises.es: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura.
Tomé una decisión difícil.

exercises.prompt: I'd like to ___ a complaint about the service.

exercises.es: Hizo un gran esfuerzo.

lessons.title: Elipsis y sustitución: so do I, neither, do so

sections.heading: Yo también, yo tampoco
body: So + auxiliar + sujeto para sumarse a una afirmación (I love jazz. So do I.); neither / nor + auxiliar + sujeto para una negativa (I can't swim. Neither can I.). El auxiliar copia el de la frase: so am I, so did we, neither have they.

examples.en: She's left-handed, and so is her brother.
examples.es: Ella es zurda, y su hermano también.

examples.en: I didn't enjoy it, and neither did Tom.
examples.es: No me gustó, y a Tom tampoco.

examples.en: We've already eaten. So have we.
examples.es: Ya hemos comido. Nosotros también.

rows: Neither do I. / Nor do I.

sections.heading: Evitar repetir el verbo
body: Tras un auxiliar se omite lo repetido: Can you come? I'd love to (= to come). Have you finished? I have. Do so sustituye a una acción completa en registro formal: Those who wish to leave may do so. So y not sustituyen oraciones tras think, hope, expect, suppose, be afraid: I think so. I hope not.

examples.en: Will it rain? I hope not.
examples.es: ¿Lloverá? Espero que no.

examples.en: Did she pass? I believe so.
examples.es: ¿Aprobó? Creo que sí.

examples.en: You can keep the book if you want to.
examples.es: Puedes quedarte el libro si quieres.

examples.en: Anyone wishing to apply should do so before Friday.
examples.es: Quien desee presentarse debe hacerlo antes del viernes.

sections.heading: One, ones y that of
body: One / ones evitan repetir un sustantivo contable: I need a pen. Have you got one? The red ones are nicer. En registro formal, that of / those of: The climate here is milder than that of the north.

examples.en: Which shoes? The black ones.
examples.es: ¿Qué zapatos? Los negros.

examples.en: Our results were better than those of last year.
examples.es: Nuestros resultados fueron mejores que los del año pasado.

sections.tip: Ones no sustituye incontables: «some sugar… the brown one» es un error; se dice the brown kind o the brown sugar.

exercises.prompt: I've never been to Japan. ___
She works from home, and ___.
Is he coming? I ___.
I can't cook. ___ can I. (tampoco)
Which bag do you want? The small ___.

exercises.es: A mí tampoco me gustó la película.
Yo también estoy cansado.
¿Vendrá? Espero que sí.
answers: Will he come? I hope so.
Will she come? I hope so.
Is he coming? I hope so.

lessons.title: Verbos que cambian de sentido: remember, stop, try, regret
lessons.summary: Remember to lock no es remember locking.

sections.heading: Remember, forget, regret
body: Remember / forget + to: acordarse de hacer algo (futuro respecto al recuerdo): Remember to buy milk. Remember / forget + -ing: recordar haber hecho algo (pasado): I remember locking the door. Regret + to: lamentar comunicar algo (formal): We regret to inform you. Regret + -ing: arrepentirse de algo hecho: I regret saying that.

examples.en: Did you remember to post the letter?
examples.es: ¿Te acordaste de enviar la carta?

examples.en: I'll never forget meeting her.
examples.es: Nunca olvidaré el día que la conocí.

examples.en: We regret to inform you that the flight is cancelled.
examples.es: Lamentamos informarle de que el vuelo está cancelado.

examples.en: He regrets leaving school so early.
examples.es: Se arrepiente de haber dejado los estudios tan pronto.

sections.heading: Stop, try, mean, go on
body: Stop + -ing: dejar de hacer (She stopped smoking). Stop + to: parar para hacer (She stopped to smoke). Try + to: intentar algo difícil (I tried to open it). Try + -ing: probar una alternativa (Try turning it off and on). Mean + to: tener intención (I didn't mean to hurt you). Mean + -ing: implicar (Moving means leaving my friends). Go on + -ing: seguir; go on + to: pasar a lo siguiente.

examples.en: I tried to call you, but there was no signal.
examples.es: Intenté llamarte, pero no había cobertura.

examples.en: If the door won't open, try pushing it.
examples.es: Si la puerta no abre, prueba a empujarla.

examples.en: Taking the job would mean moving to Berlin.
examples.es: Aceptar el trabajo supondría mudarse a Berlín.

examples.en: After the song, she went on to talk about her new album.
examples.es: Tras la canción, pasó a hablar de su nuevo disco.

sections.tip: Stop to smoke y stop smoking significan lo contrario: elige bien.

sections.heading: Need, want y verbos de percepción
body: Need + -ing con sentido pasivo: The car needs washing (= needs to be washed). See, hear, watch, feel + objeto + verbo base (acción completa) o + -ing (en curso): I saw him cross the road / I saw him crossing the road.

examples.en: These shirts need ironing.
examples.es: Estas camisas necesitan planchado.

examples.en: I heard someone knock at the door.
examples.es: Oí a alguien llamar a la puerta.

examples.en: We watched the sun setting over the sea.
examples.es: Vimos el sol poniéndose sobre el mar.

exercises.prompt: Please remember ___ the lights when you leave.
I'll never forget ___ the Grand Canyon for the first time.
We stopped ___ some petrol.
Try ___ (restart) the computer; that usually works.
I didn't mean ___ (upset) you.

exercises.es: Lamentamos informarle de que la tienda cierra.
Dejó de fumar hace años.
answers: She gave up smoking years ago.

exercises.es: Me arrepiento de haberle gritado.
answers: I regret having shouted at him.

lessons.title: Likely, bound to, may well: graduar la probabilidad

sections.heading: Escala de certeza
body: De más a menos seguro: be bound to / be sure to / be certain to (seguro que), will definitely, be likely to / probably, may well (es muy posible), may / might / could, be unlikely to, there's little chance (of), won't possibly (de ninguna manera).

examples.en: He's bound to be late; he always is.
examples.es: Seguro que llega tarde; siempre lo hace.

examples.en: Prices are likely to rise next year.
examples.es: Es probable que los precios suban el año que viene.

examples.en: She may well change her mind.
examples.es: Es muy posible que cambie de opinión.

examples.en: It's highly unlikely that they'll agree.
examples.es: Es muy poco probable que accedan.

rows: be bound to, be sure to, definitely
be likely to, probably, I expect
may well, may, might, could, possibly
be unlikely to, I doubt, there's little chance

sections.heading: Likely y unlikely en frases
body: It is likely that + oración / sujeto + be likely to + verbo: It's likely that she'll win = She's likely to win. Con grados: quite likely, very likely, highly unlikely, more than likely.

examples.en: The meeting is likely to be postponed.
examples.es: Es probable que la reunión se posponga.

examples.en: It's quite unlikely that he saw us.
examples.es: Es bastante improbable que nos viera.

examples.en: They're more than likely to accept.
examples.es: Es más que probable que acepten.

sections.heading: Hablar con cautela
body: Para no comprometerse: I'd say…, I'd imagine…, as far as I know, presumably, apparently, it seems, chances are (lo más probable es que), the odds are.

examples.en: Chances are he's already heard the news.
examples.es: Lo más probable es que ya se haya enterado.

examples.en: Presumably they'll send a confirmation.
examples.es: Es de suponer que enviarán una confirmación.

examples.en: As far as I know, the shop is still open.
examples.es: Que yo sepa, la tienda sigue abierta.

sections.tip: Probably va después de will y antes de won't: She'll probably come; she probably won't come.

exercises.prompt: Look at the queue. We ___ wait at least an hour.
It's ___ that the match will be cancelled; the pitch is flooded.
They ___ well have left already.
She's ___ to be promoted this year. (probable)
___ are he won't notice. (lo más probable es que)

exercises.es: Es muy poco probable que vengan.
Seguro que llueve mañana.
answers: It is bound to rain tomorrow.

exercises.es: Es probable que el tren llegue tarde.
answers: The train is likely to be late.
It's likely that the train will be late.
The train will probably be late.

lessons.title: Fronting y orden marcado
lessons.summary: Here comes the bus; off we go; this I cannot accept.

sections.heading: Adelantar para enfatizar
body: En inglés el orden normal es sujeto-verbo-objeto, pero se puede adelantar un elemento para destacarlo o para enlazar con lo anterior: This I cannot accept. That much is clear. Some things you never forget. Suele ser enfático o literario.

examples.en: Some mistakes you only make once.
examples.es: Algunos errores solo se cometen una vez.

examples.en: That I can believe.
examples.es: Eso sí me lo creo.

examples.en: Most of the money they spent on the house.
examples.es: La mayor parte del dinero la gastaron en la casa.

sections.heading: Here, there y adverbios de lugar
body: Con here, there y adverbios de lugar o movimiento al inicio, el verbo va antes del sujeto cuando el sujeto es un sustantivo: Here comes the bus. There goes my train. Up went the balloon. Con un pronombre no hay inversión: Here it comes. Off we go.

examples.en: Here comes the teacher!
examples.es: ¡Ahí viene el profesor!

examples.en: There stood an old castle on the hill.
examples.es: Allí se alzaba un viejo castillo en la colina.

examples.en: Down came the rain.
examples.es: Y se puso a llover a cántaros.

examples.en: Away they went.
examples.es: Y se marcharon.

sections.heading: Participios y adjetivos al inicio
body: En descripciones formales o literarias un participio o adjetivo puede abrir la frase con inversión: Attached is the report you requested. Standing in the doorway was a tall man. Equally important is the cost.

examples.en: Enclosed are the documents you asked for.
examples.es: Adjuntos van los documentos que solicitó.

examples.en: Sitting on the bench was an old woman.
examples.es: Sentada en el banco había una anciana.

examples.en: Also present at the meeting were two lawyers.
examples.es: También estaban presentes en la reunión dos abogados.

sections.tip: El fronting es un recurso puntual: usado en cada frase, el texto suena artificial.

exercises.prompt: Here ___ the bus!
Here ___! (pronombre)
___ is the invoice for your order.
Off ___ went, without saying goodbye. (ellos)
Standing at the door ___ a policeman. (verbo)

exercises.es: Algunas cosas nunca se olvidan.
Ahí va mi tren.
Adjunto va el informe.

lessons.title: Nominalización y estilo académico
lessons.summary: De «decidieron» a «la decisión»: el inglés de los informes.

sections.heading: Verbos y adjetivos que se vuelven sustantivos
body: En textos formales las acciones se expresan como sustantivos: They decided → their decision; it failed → its failure; we analysed → our analysis; grew rapidly → rapid growth. Permite frases más densas e impersonales.

examples.en: The company's decision to expand surprised investors.
examples.es: La decisión de la empresa de expandirse sorprendió a los inversores.

examples.en: A thorough analysis of the data is needed.
examples.es: Se necesita un análisis exhaustivo de los datos.

examples.en: The rapid growth of the city has caused problems.
examples.es: El rápido crecimiento de la ciudad ha causado problemas.

sections.heading: Verbos ligeros con nominalizaciones
body: Las nominalizaciones van con verbos como make, carry out, conduct, reach, undergo, give: carry out research, conduct a survey, reach a conclusion, undergo a transformation, give consideration to.

examples.en: The team carried out an investigation.
examples.es: El equipo llevó a cabo una investigación.

examples.en: No agreement was reached.
examples.es: No se alcanzó ningún acuerdo.

examples.en: The building underwent extensive renovation.
examples.es: El edificio fue sometido a una amplia reforma.

sections.heading: Impersonalidad y cautela académica
body: It is widely believed that…, It could be argued that…, There is evidence to suggest…, This would appear to indicate… Sujetos abstractos: The findings suggest…, Figure 2 shows…

examples.en: It could be argued that the policy has failed.
examples.es: Podría argumentarse que la política ha fracasado.

examples.en: The findings suggest a link between diet and mood.
examples.es: Los resultados sugieren una relación entre dieta y estado de ánimo.

examples.en: There is little evidence to support this claim.
examples.es: Hay pocas pruebas que respalden esta afirmación.

sections.tip: Las nominalizaciones en exceso oscurecen: en un correo normal, «we decided» es mejor que «a decision was made».

exercises.prompt: The ___ of the bridge took five years. (construct)
Scientists ___ an experiment to test the theory.
There has been a significant ___ in sales.
Their ___ (fail) to act cost them the contract. (sustantivo)
The committee ___ a conclusion after three hours. (verbo ligero, pasado)

Se necesita un análisis más detallado.
answers: A more detailed analysis is needed.
A more detailed analysis is required.

answers: The findings suggest a link between the two.

lessons.title: Preposiciones dependientes y expresiones fijas
lessons.summary: Depend on, interested in, on behalf of, in terms of.

sections.heading: Verbo + preposición
body: Muchos verbos exigen una preposición concreta: depend on, rely on, insist on, apologise for, blame for, accuse of, approve of, consist of, belong to, object to, succeed in, participate in, result in, lead to, cope with, deal with.

examples.en: It all depends on the weather.
examples.es: Todo depende del tiempo.

examples.en: She was accused of lying.
examples.es: La acusaron de mentir.

examples.en: The talks resulted in an agreement.
examples.es: Las conversaciones desembocaron en un acuerdo.

examples.en: I can't cope with so much pressure.
examples.es: No puedo con tanta presión.

sections.heading: Adjetivo + preposición
body: Interested in, good/bad at, afraid of, fond of, aware of, capable of, keen on, proud of, responsible for, famous for, different from, similar to, married to, dependent on.

examples.en: I'm not very good at maths.
examples.es: No se me dan muy bien las matemáticas.

examples.en: She's keen on photography.
examples.es: A ella le apasiona la fotografía.

examples.en: He is fully aware of the consequences.
examples.es: Él es plenamente consciente de las consecuencias.

sections.tip: Depende de = depend on (no «depend of»); consistir en = consist of (no «consist in»).

sections.heading: Expresiones fijas de registro formal
body: On behalf of (en nombre de), in terms of (en cuanto a), with regard to / regarding (respecto a), in the light of (a la luz de), in accordance with (de acuerdo con), at the expense of (a costa de), on the grounds that (alegando que), by means of (mediante).

examples.en: On behalf of the team, thank you.
examples.es: En nombre del equipo, gracias.

examples.en: In terms of cost, the second option is better.
examples.es: En cuanto al coste, la segunda opción es mejor.

examples.en: The request was refused on the grounds that it was late.
examples.es: La solicitud fue rechazada alegando que llegó tarde.

exercises.prompt: The success of the project depends ___ funding.
She apologised ___ the delay.
He's very fond ___ his grandchildren.
The menu consists ___ five courses.
___ behalf of the company, I would like to thank you. (preposición)

exercises.es: En cuanto al precio, es la mejor opción.
Soy consciente del problema.
answers: I am aware of the problem.

exercises.es: Todo depende de ti.

lessons.title: Comprensión lectora y auditiva
lessons.summary: Ensayos, crónicas y conferencias: estructura, tono y matiz.

sections.heading: La estructura del argumento
body: Un ensayo plantea una tesis, la apoya con pruebas, concede algo al contrario y concluye. Localiza esas piezas: la tesis suele ir al principio o al final del primer párrafo; las concesiones empiezan con granted, admittedly, it is true that; la conclusión, con therefore, ultimately, in short.

examples.en: Granted, the policy has reduced costs; the question is at what price.
examples.es: Es cierto que la política ha reducido costes; la cuestión es a qué precio.

examples.en: Ultimately, the evidence points in one direction.
examples.es: En última instancia, las pruebas apuntan en una dirección.

examples.en: It is true that early results were promising.
examples.es: Es verdad que los primeros resultados fueron prometedores.

sections.heading: Tono e ironía
body: El tono se reconoce en la elección de palabras: understatement (quitar hierro: not exactly a success), hipérbole, ironía (decir lo contrario de lo que se piensa). Si una afirmación parece absurda tomada al pie de la letra, probablemente es irónica. Las preguntas de tono ofrecen opciones como critical, sceptical, nostalgic, detached, admiring.

examples.en: The meeting was not exactly a triumph.
examples.es: La reunión no fue precisamente un triunfo.

examples.en: Another brilliant idea from head office.
examples.es: Otra idea brillante de la central (irónico).

examples.en: He spoke with the quiet confidence of someone who had never been wrong, or had never noticed.
examples.es: Habló con la serena confianza de quien nunca se ha equivocado, o nunca se ha dado cuenta.

sections.heading: Escuchar con atención al matiz
body: En conferencias y entrevistas largas, las ideas se califican constantemente: broadly speaking, with one exception, up to a point. Distingue lo que el hablante afirma, lo que atribuye a otros (some would argue) y lo que descarta. Las preguntas suelen apuntar a esa diferencia.

examples.en: Some would argue that the reforms came too late; I'm not sure that's fair.
examples.es: Algunos dirían que las reformas llegaron tarde; no estoy seguro de que sea justo.

examples.en: Broadly speaking, the data support the theory, with one notable exception.
examples.es: En términos generales, los datos apoyan la teoría, con una excepción notable.

examples.en: That's true up to a point.
examples.es: Eso es cierto hasta cierto punto.

exercises.title: Essay: on silence
exercises.text: We treat silence as an absence, a gap to be filled with music, chatter or the glow of a screen. Yet for most of human history, silence was the default and noise the exception. It is tempting to blame technology, and admittedly our devices make noise effortless. But the deeper change is cultural: we have come to regard a quiet mind as an idle one. Until we unlearn that, no app will give us back what we have given away.

questions.prompt: What is the author's main claim?
options: We now see silence as emptiness and a quiet mind as idle
Noise has always been the default

questions.prompt: How does the author treat the role of technology?
options: Admits it plays a part but sees a deeper cause

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence suggest?
options: An app could solve the problem
The solution is cultural, not technical

exercises.title: Report: the village school
exercises.text: When the village school was threatened with closure, the campaign to save it was led, improbably, by residents with no children: retired teachers, a farmer, the owner of the pub. Their argument was less about education than about what a village is for. A school, they said, is where a place rehearses its future. The council, perhaps sensing that it had lost the argument before it began, quietly withdrew the proposal.

questions.prompt: Why is the leadership of the campaign described as 'improbable'?
options: The campaigners had no children at the school

questions.prompt: What was the campaigners' main argument?
options: The role of the school in the village's future

questions.prompt: How did the council respond?

exercises.title: Column: the end of the expert?
exercises.text: It has become fashionable to declare that we have had enough of experts. The sentiment is understandable: experts have been wrong, sometimes spectacularly, and rarely with consequences for themselves. Yet the alternative, trusting whoever speaks loudest, has a poor record too. The sensible position is neither reverence nor contempt but accountability: expertise that explains itself, admits uncertainty and can be checked.

questions.prompt: What is the author's attitude to the slogan about experts?
What does the author see as the problem with the alternative?
options: Trusting the loudest voices has a poor record

questions.prompt: What does the author propose?

exercises.title: Notice: research participants wanted
exercises.text: The Department of Psychology is recruiting adults aged 25 to 60 for a study on sleep and decision-making. Participants will wear a small wrist monitor for two weeks and complete three online sessions of about forty minutes each. Those with diagnosed sleep disorders are not eligible, as the study concerns typical sleep patterns. Participation is voluntary and can be withdrawn at any time without explanation; a modest payment is offered on completion.

questions.prompt: Who is not eligible?
options: People over 60 and people with diagnosed sleep disorders

questions.prompt: What will participants have to do?
options: Wear a wrist monitor and complete online sessions
Keep a diary for a year

questions.prompt: What is said about withdrawing from the study?
options: It is possible at any time without explanation

exercises.title: Conference talk on cities
exercises.text: Thank you. I want to challenge an assumption that underlies most urban planning: that density is the enemy of quality of life. Broadly speaking, the data show the opposite. Residents of dense, walkable neighbourhoods report higher satisfaction, with one notable exception: families with young children, who consistently prioritise space over proximity. So the question for planners is not whether to build densely, but how to do so without pushing those families out.

questions.prompt: What assumption does the speaker challenge?
options: That density harms quality of life

questions.prompt: What exception does she mention?
What question does she pose to planners?
options: How to build densely without pushing families out

exercises.title: Interview with a translator
exercises.text: People imagine translation as a kind of dictionary work, and I understand why, but the dictionary is the least of it. The hard part is tone: a joke that lands in one language dies in another. Some would say that makes translation impossible; I'd say it makes it a craft. You lose something in every sentence, yes. The skill is choosing what to lose.

questions.prompt: What misconception does the translator describe?
options: That jokes are easy to translate

questions.prompt: How does she respond to the idea that translation is impossible?
options: She calls it a craft instead

questions.prompt: What does she say the skill consists of?

exercises.title: A museum audio guide
exercises.text: The painting in front of you was long attributed to a pupil of the master, until cleaning in 1998 revealed a signature under two centuries of varnish. Not everyone was persuaded: a signature can be added, and several scholars still consider the brushwork too hesitant. The museum's position, for now, is cautious: the label reads 'attributed to', which is as far as the evidence allows.

questions.prompt: What did the cleaning in 1998 reveal?
Why are some scholars not persuaded?
What does the label say?

exercises.title: Panel discussion on remote work
exercises.text: Let me push back on that. The claim that remote work hurts creativity rests on a handful of studies that measured, essentially, how often people bumped into each other. That's true up to a point: chance encounters matter. But the same studies ignore the hours lost to commuting and the people who never applied for jobs in cities they couldn't afford. On balance, I'd call the evidence mixed rather than damning.

questions.prompt: What did the studies he criticises actually measure?
options: How often people met by chance

questions.prompt: What do those studies ignore, according to the speaker?
options: Commuting time and people excluded by housing costs

questions.prompt: How does he describe the evidence?

exam.title: Review: a biography
exam.text: Biographers of the composer have tended to divide into admirers and prosecutors. This new account does something rarer: it declines to take sides, and is more interesting for it. The author lets the contradictions stand: the generous teacher and the vindictive colleague, the atheist who wrote his most moving music for the church. If the book has a flaw, it is a reluctance to speculate where the record is silent, which leaves some chapters more inventory than portrait.

questions.prompt: What is unusual about this biography?
What contradictions does the author leave unresolved?
options: Between the composer's generosity and vindictiveness, and his atheism and church music

questions.prompt: What flaw does the reviewer identify?

exam.title: Expert panel on language learning
exam.text: The idea that adults can't learn languages well is, broadly speaking, a myth, though like most myths it has a grain of truth. Children acquire accent more easily, that much is clear. But in vocabulary, in grammar, in reading, adults regularly outperform them, given the same hours. Some would argue that adults simply never get those hours. I'd say that's the real finding: it's not the brain that's the obstacle, it's the calendar.

questions.prompt: What grain of truth does the speaker concede?
In what areas do adults outperform children?
What does the speaker identify as the real obstacle?
